current_selector.inherited_semantics: discover recognized matches -> choose minimum rank per target -> post-filter selected edge to allowed codecs

theorem: A disallowed codec may be skipped before decode only when its known rank is strictly worse than every known allowed codec rank. If the allowed set contains an unknown/unranked codec, disable this pruning conservatively. Better-ranked disallowed codecs remain observable because they can mask worse-ranked allowed candidates under choose-min-then-filter semantics.
shipping_consequence: With current allowed={gzip,zstd}, xz is the only recognized rank-safe pre-decode skip.
negative_control: If allowed={gzip} and both zstd+gzip match, full discovery selects zstd then post-filter emits no edge. Blindly skipping all disallowed codecs would expose gzip and change semantics.
implementation_boundary: Full discovery remains default when allowed_codecs is omitted.
Preserve the existing post-filter as semantic authority even after pre-decode pruning.
Unknown allowed codec ranks disable pruning rather than extrapolating rank dominance.
Record skipped sidecar count/stored bytes as observability, not archive metadata.
claim_boundary: Selector algebra/property evidence only. Exact-head implementation tests and hosted product A/B remain mandatory before product/release credit.
